# Lore

## Task Pipeline

**Live agent MCP access**: this is the only context path now; agent *pods* get a
**live, scoped** Lore MCP for the whole run via the shared `lore-mcp` HTTP
gateway. An agent recipe
carries `resources.mcp_servers: [{ name: lore, transport: http, headers_secret:
lore-mcp-auth }]` and drops `lore_create_pipeline_task`; the ai-agent-subsystem
controller renders it into `claude --mcp-config`; for a Gemini run the init merges
them into gemini-cli's user settings (`/agent/.gemini/settings.json`, subsystem v0.11.3:
the system-scope file v0.11.2 used is refused for a uid-1000 directory, so every Gemini
pod before 2026-09-23 ran with 0 tools). The pod can search
memory/context and record targeted memory throughout the run. The
gateway is reachable at a public `:443` host be…

Gemini pods still have NO Lore MCP after subsystem v0.11.2 (lore #2133, subsystem #240): gemini-cli prints "Security Warning: Skipping system settings file '/agent/.ai-agent/gemini-settings.json': Parent directory is not owned by root (uid 0). Current uid: 1000" and starts with "init … (0 tools)"; 4 Gemini runs after controller ce54c7a0 made zero MCP calls. Filed re-cinq/ai-agent-subsystem#245: write to the user settings $HOME/.gemini/settings.json instead of GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH (system path needs root-owned dir; pod is uid 1000). Verify a fix by the run's init tool count > 0 and mcp_lore_* tool_call rows at https://lore-agent-events.gcp.re-cinq.com/api/agent-events/<runId>.

Side finding: the recheck line fires on every push; a rebase + CI prettier commit produced 3 Pro review…

session-summary/2026-09-23-gemini-mcp-v0.11.3-proven

Gemini agent pods now reach the Lore MCP (proven 2026-09-23 ~21:20 UTC). Chain: subsystem #246 (init merges mcpServers into gemini-cli USER settings /agent/.gemini/settings.json via `ai-agent-init mcp-settings <file> <servers>`; the v0.11.2 system-scope file was refused for a uid-1000 dir), #247 changelog cut, tag v0.11.3, #249 agent-contracts bump 0.11.3 + manual publish-contracts dispatch, lore #2144 chart pins (controller sha256:77307751…, agent sha256:56ce7fa5…), deploy-ai-agents green 21:15 UTC. Proof: code-review run f0e87e9e (lore #2145) made mcp_lore_lore_assemble_context x1, mcp_lore_lore_search_memory x2, mcp_lore_lore_get_ci_failures x1.

# ADR-032: Split the local MCP adapter from the remote HTTP API

## Amendment (2026-08): `apps/mcp-server` gains a third deployable shape — the HTTP gateway

Decision 1 cast `apps/mcp-server` as **local-only** (the stdio MCP adapter on a developer laptop). It
now also runs as a **shared cluster deployable**: the `lore-mcp` gateway that serves agent pods their
live Lore tools over MCP-over-HTTP. Same code, same `buildMcpServer`, a new transport — `LORE_MCP_HTTP=1`
mounts the SDK's `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` instead of stdio, and `LORE_MCP_SERVER_MODE=agent`
omits the laptop-only + task-creating tools. The two runtime shapes of `apps/mcp-server` are therefore:

**Why.** gemini-cli takes no MCP flag; it reads MCP servers from its settings. The subsystem rendered a recipe's `mcp_servers` only for Claude, so every Gemini agent pod, including every code review since the review moved to Gemini 3.1 Pro, ran with no Lore MCP at all: no `lore_assemble_context`, no memory, no CI verdict. Measured on today's transcripts: 13 Gemini review runs made zero MCP calls, and one tried `command -v lore_assemble_context` in the shell. v0.11.2 (re-cinq/ai-agent-subsystem#240) has the init write the servers to a settings file of its own and points the CLI at it through `GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH`; the header stays the `${LORE_MCP_AUTH}` reference the Claude path already uses, so no token reaches disk.

Author: gedaiu

Link: https://github.com/re-cinq/lore/issues/2146

## What happens

The run page's init line (`init gemini-3.1-pro-preview (0 tools)`) reads a tool count from `ev.tools` in the vendor's init event ([agent-run-events.ts:35](apps/floor/src/work/agent/agent-run-events.ts#L35)). gemini-cli's init event carries no `tools` array, so every Gemini run reports 0 tools, including run `f0e87e9e-8b7e-4ad2-8534-5696a9f0abcf` (review of #2145) which then made four `mcp_lore_*` calls.

## Why it matters

Today that line is the fastest signal for "did this pod get the Lore MCP", and for Gemini it is always wrong. It hid subsystem #245 for a…
